slides.headline: Raise3D launched two giant printers
body: Raise3D makes professional 3D printers and the free ideaMaker slicer.
On Nov 11 it announced the T450 and T700: big printers with a heated chamber, which it calls the most affordable of their kind.

slides.headline: How big?
hits: Hot end up to 420°C, bed up to 120°C
Fibre-ready: PET CF, PPA CF and PPS CF

slides.headline: Two filaments, one nozzle
body: TwinFlow feeds two filament paths into one nozzle: up to 600 mm/s in Raise3D’s own tests, or two materials for dissolvable supports.
The heated chamber keeps big ABS and nylon parts from warping, and vents open for PLA.

slides.headline: Big parts in one piece
body: Large jigs, moulds and prototypes can print whole instead of being split and glued.
Raise3D’s example: a scoliosis brace, which has to be one piece to be strong enough.

slides.headline: From $4,999
body: T450: US$4,999, shipping by the end of December.
T700: US$15,999, expected by the end of January. Both are on show at Formnext in Frankfurt, Nov 17–20.

slides.headline: Not a home printer
body: At $4,999 this is a business machine, not a hobby upgrade.
slides.take: Most of our jobs fit on our Bambu and Snapmaker beds. For a part bigger than that, a printer like this beats cutting it up.
